newsitem.title: FRANCE: Carrefour raises stake in GMB.
newsitem.headline: Carrefour raises stake in GMB.

text.p: French retailer Carrefour said on Thursday it had raised its stake in the holding company controlling the Cora retail group to 41.4 percent, fuelling speculation of a creeping takeover.
Carrefour said in a statement that it bought 8.1 percent of the holding company GMB on Tuesday on top of a 33.3 percent stake purchased last week, for a total of 3.1 billion francs ($589.4 million).

A spokesman for Carrefour declined to say whether it was seeking control of Cora. He said that in both instances, Carrefour had been approached by members of the Bouriez family seeking to sell shares in GMB. The family controls GMB.
Shares in Carrefour rose 5.03 percent to close at 3,277 francs as investors applauded its bid to reinforce its presence in the rapidly consolidating French hypermarkets industry.

The consolidation, driven by a strict retail law enacted this year making it difficult for big suburban stores to open new outlets or expand existing ones, began in the autumn with the hostile takeover of Docks de France by Auchan.

Stock market specialists said the parallels between the two situations were striking. "In both cases, the move was initially described as a defensive tactic (to thwart another bidder) and then they increased (their holdings)," one analyst said.
Another analyst said Carrefour appeared to be amassing shares in GMB quickly to deter a rival bid by a white knight that could drive up the cost of the deal.
Analysts said the price paid so far by Carrefour was not considered expensive.

The two companies' activities complement each other geographically. Carrefour has 117 stores in France but a thin presence in the northeast and in neighbouring Belgium, where Cora's 55 markets are concentrated.
Cora also holds 41 percent of Belgian retailer Louis Delhaize.
-- Noelle Mennella, Paris Newsroom, +33 1 4221 5452 ($ = 5.26 French Francs)
